heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷四 (子上) · 29 … 4

items.text: While your parents live, serve them with love and reverence; when they die, carry through your duty to them with grief and proper rites.
items.quote: 生事愛敬，死事哀戚 — In life serve with love and respect; in death with mourning.

items.text: Mourn your dead parent with genuine grief, but after three days eat, do not let grief destroy your nature, and do not prolong mourning beyond three years.
items.quote: 三日而食…毀不滅性…喪不過三年 — After three days eat; do not destroy your nature; mourning does not exceed three years.

items.text: Provide the coffin, grave-clothes and offerings; wail as you send them away, and lay the body to rest.
items.quote: 為之棺槨衣衾而舉之…哀以送之，安厝之 — Provide coffin and grave-clothes… send them away with grief and lay them to rest.

items.text: Divine the grave site before laying your parent to rest.
items.quote: 卜其宅兆而安厝之 — Divine the grave site and lay him to rest.
items.conflict: Scripture forbids divination and omens (Deut 18:10); burial needs no divination.

items.text: Erect the ancestral temple and offer spring and autumn sacrifices, remembering them at the due times.
items.quote: 為之宗廟，以鬼享之。春秋祭祀，以時思之 — Make an ancestral temple and present seasonal sacrifices.
items.conflict: Worship belongs to God alone (Exod 20:3-5); offerings to the dead are forbidden.

items.text: Sacrifice to the dead as if they were present, with outward offerings and inward sincerity; enter the shrine as though you saw their place and heard their voice.
items.quote: 祭如在。君子事死如事生，事亡如事存…入室，僾然必有見乎其位 — Sacrifice as if present; serve the dead as the living… upon entering, seem to see their place.
items.conflict: Scripture forbids sacrifices to the dead; remember the departed without worshiping them.

items.text: Complete the full three-year mourning and refuse public office or ordinary duties until the mourning is finished.
items.quote: 睿宗起復為工部侍郎，颋固辭…上乃聽其終制 — Su Ting firmly declined appointment and was allowed to finish mourning.

items.text: When sacrificing to ancestors, personally wash the vessels even in old age, so that your remembrance may be sincere.
items.quote: 年七十餘，享祖考，猶親滌器 — Past seventy, he still personally washed vessels for ancestral offerings.
items.conflict: Offerings to ancestors are forbidden; love for ancestors must not become worship.

items.text: Preserve the body, hair and skin your parents gave you unharmed; avoid dangerous paths, boating, swimming, and every needless risk.
items.quote: 身體髮膚，受之父母，不敢毀傷 — Body, hair and skin are received from parents; do not injure them.

items.text: Rescue your parents from danger or punishment, even at the cost or risk of your own life.
items.quote: 況救親於危難乎！古以死徇其親者多矣 — How much more when parents are in peril; many ancients died for them.

items.text: Remonstrate gently with your parents when they are wrong; do not obey an unrighteous command, but remain respectful and continue to plead.
items.quote: 事父母幾諫。見誌不從，又敬不違，勞而不怨 — Serve parents with gentle remonstrance; if they do not listen, remain respectful and uncomplaining.

items.text: Endure mild correction, but if a parent's blow would kill you, flee, so that you do not let your parent kill you and become a murderer.
items.quote: 小捶則待過，大杖則逃走 — Receive the small blow; flee from the staff that would kill.

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷三 (父母 父 母) · 35 … 49

items.text: Train your child in propriety and cultivate his virtue, not just his body, so he will not enter evil and can bear loyal service.
items.quote: 非徒鞠育其身使不罹水火，又當養其德使不入於邪惡 — Not only raise his body to avoid harm, but cultivate his virtue to keep him from evil.

items.text: Use your inherited office and salary to bless your father's kin for his sake; do not keep the benefit for yourself.
items.quote: 當散贍六姻，為先君之惠，奈何獨擅其利，以為富貴乎 — Distribute it to your six relations as your late father's kindness; how can you claim it alone?

items.text: Honor your late husband by remaining chaste, plainly dressed, frugal, and home-keeping rather than adorning yourself and making idle visits.
items.quote: 自初寡，便不禦脂粉，常服大練... 未嘗輒出門閣 — From early widowhood she wore no cosmetics, always coarse silk, and never idly left the gate.

items.text: When your child sends home wealth from office, do not merely rejoice; ask whether it was gained righteously.
items.quote: 父母但知忻悅，不問金帛所從來。若以非道得之，此乃為盜而未發者耳 — Parents just rejoice and do not ask where gold and silk came from; if gotten wrongly, it is theft not yet exposed.

items.text: Be loyal and incorrupt in office, so that your parents need not choke with shame at their table.
items.quote: 茍不能忠清，雖日殺三牲，吾猶食之不下咽也 — If you cannot be loyal and pure, even if you kill three animals daily, I still cannot swallow it.

items.text: Serve your mother with daily reverence and submit to her correction even when you hold high office.
items.quote: 景讓事之，終日常兢兢 — Li Jingrang served her all day in constant fear and caution.

items.text: Correct your child's faults even in high office; do not let him use state law as an instrument of his anger to kill the innocent.
items.quote: 國家刑法，豈得以為汝喜怒之資，妄殺無罪之人乎 — How can the state's laws be used as fuel for your anger to kill innocent persons?

items.text: Love and bring up a child not born from you with wholehearted care, not holding back because the child is not your flesh.
items.quote: 人未必當自生子，但患愛養不至耳... 盡心撫育，勞瘁過於所生 — One need not bear one's own child; only fear love and nurture are insufficient. She labored more than if he had been her own.

items.text: Be filial and affectionate toward the mother who raised you, with no rift or coldness between you.
items.quote: 母子慈愛，始終無纖介之間 — Mother and son were loving from beginning to end, without the slightest estrangement.

items.text: Love your stepchildren as your own, and lead them with propriety and justice, not partiality for your own children.
items.quote: 繼母如母，為人母而不能愛其子，可謂慈乎？親其親而偏其假，可謂義乎 — A stepmother is as a mother; not loving his child is not kindness; loving your own and favoring stepchildren is not righteousness.

items.text: Keep the promise you made to your dying husband concerning his children; do not let private love override public faithfulness.
items.quote: 今既受人之托，許人以諾，豈可忘人之托而不信其諾耶 — Having received his trust and made a promise, how can you forget it and break your word?

items.text: Honor and love a kind stepmother; receive her training instead of despising her.
items.quote: 五子親慈母雍雍若一 — The five sons cherished their kind stepmother in harmony as one family.

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷二 (祖) · 1 … 10

items.text: Train your children in righteousness and govern your household by ritual and law; do not merely amass wealth for them.
items.quote: 以義方訓其子，以禮法齊其家 — Train your son in righteousness and regulate your household by ritual.

items.text: Leave your descendants virtue, propriety, integrity, and thrift rather than stored-up wealth.
items.quote: 聖人遺子孫以德以禮，賢人遺子孫以廉以儉 — Sages leave descendants virtue and rites; worthies leave integrity and thrift.

items.text: Love your children by teaching them right conduct; do not lead them into pride, extravagance, lust, or idleness.
items.quote: 愛子教之以義方，弗納於邪。驕奢淫逸，所自邪也 — To love a child is to teach him what is right and not let him enter evil.

items.text: Begin training a child from infancy; do not wait until he is grown.
items.quote: 故自為赤子，而教固已行矣 — From infancy, teaching has already begun.

items.text: Do not deceive a child; if you make him a promise, keep it.
items.quote: 曾子即烹豕以食儿，曰：‘毋教儿欺也。’ — Zengzi cooked the pig for the child, saying, ‘Do not teach the child to deceive.’

items.text: Love your child without doting on him; command him without display; guide him by the Way without forcing him.
items.quote: 愛之而勿面，使之而勿貌，遵之以道而勿強言 — Love him but do not show partiality; use him but do not put on airs; lead him by the Way but do not force words.

items.text: Surround your children with upright people so that they see, hear, and do what is right.
items.quote: 左右前後皆正人也 — Those around him, before and behind, are all upright.

items.text: Practice frugality in your household so that its members do not become accustomed to luxury and unable to endure hardship.
items.quote: 人情由儉入奢則易，由奢入儉則難 — Human nature: from thrift to luxury is easy, from luxury to thrift is hard.

items.text: Tend to your parents' physical comfort: relieve their itching and pain, hang their bedding, and arrange their pillows.
items.quote: 抑搔癢痛，懸衾篋枕 — Relieve their itching and pain; hang their bedding and put away their pillows.

items.text: When an elder takes your hand, hold it with both hands; when he speaks close by, cover your mouth to answer.
items.quote: 長者與之提攜，則兩手奉長者之手。負劍辟咡詔之，則掩口而對 — When an elder holds your hand, hold his with both hands; when he bends to speak, cover your mouth to answer.

items.text: Let elders go before you through doors and at meals; learn to yield to them.
items.quote: 出入門戶及即席飲食，必後長者 — Going out and at meals, always be after elders.

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷七 (兄 弟 姑姊妹 夫) · 17 … 9

items.text: Deal with one another with complete sincerity, not merely outward show.
items.quote: 兄弟之際，宜相與盡誠，若徒事形跡，則外雖友愛而內實乖離矣。 — Between brothers, be fully sincere; mere outward affection hides inner division.

items.text: Shield your elder brother from punishment, and let no difference of mother divide you.
items.quote: 每有杖罰，嗣立必解衣清代...兄弟茍能如此，奚異母之足患哉！ — At every beating, Sili bared himself to take it; if brothers can do this, what matter different mothers?

items.text: Go personally to meet your bride and show her deference; afterward set the household in its proper order.
items.quote: 婿冕而親迎，禦輪三周...反尊卑之正也。 — The groom in cap and gown went to meet her; then proper order was restored.

items.text: From the very beginning regulate your family by propriety, and lead your wife by your own example.
items.quote: 正家之道，靡不在初...非身率以禮義，能如是乎？ — Regulating the family lies in the beginning; without leading by propriety, could Shun have done this?

items.text: Serve your husband's parents as your daughter-in-law's duty.
items.quote: 妻天子之二女，使之行婦道於翁姑。 — He married the emperor's two daughters and made them serve his parents.

items.text: Let respectful courtesy be the beauty of your marriage.
items.quote: 夫婦之際，以敬為美。 — In marriage, honor is beautiful.

items.text: Guard her by propriety from the first; if she is prideful, fierce, and refuses correction, put her away as righteousness requires.
items.quote: 既娶而防之以禮...若妻實犯禮而出之，乃義也。 — After marrying, restrain her by ritual; if she truly violates it, to divorce is righteous.
items.conflict: Divorce is permitted only for sexual immorality (Matt 19:9); the seven grounds go beyond Scripture.

items.text: Be gentle, pure, free from jealousy, frugal, respectful, and diligent; do not make clever argument your beauty.
items.quote: 婦人專以柔順為德，不以強辯為美也。 — A woman's virtue is gentleness and compliance; not forceful argument.

items.text: Win your husband's younger brother and sister by humility and compliance, not by pride.
items.quote: 求叔妹之心，固莫尚於謙順矣。 — To gain the hearts of your husband's siblings, nothing surpasses humility and compliance.

items.text: Be constant to one husband until death, and do not adorn yourself while he is away.
items.quote: 一與之齊，終身不改...夫不在，不為容飾，禮也。 — Once joined, do not change until death; while he is away, do not dress up.

items.text: Stay with your husband if he falls gravely ill; do not leave him.
items.quote: 適人之道，一與之醮，終身不改，不幸遇惡疾...何以得去？ — Once married, never change; if he is ill, why leave?

items.text: Keep faith with your dead husband and refuse to be forced into another marriage.
items.quote: 衛世子共伯早死，其妻姜氏守義...誓而不許。 — Gongbo died young; his wife Jiang kept faith and swore not to remarry.
items.conflict: A widow is free to remarry in the Lord (1 Cor. 7:39); the tradition forbids what Scripture permits.

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷十 (舅甥 舅姑 婦 妾 乳母) · 15 … 28

items.text: Do not abandon your mother-in-law to danger; protect her even if it costs you your life.
items.quote: 況在於姑而可委棄？若萬一危禍，豈宜獨生！ — If even a neighbor in trouble is helped, how can a mother-in-law be abandoned? In danger, how should I live alone?

items.text: Fulfill the way of a wife; even a king's daughter does not stand on her rank but serves her husband's house with harmony.
items.quote: 雖則王姬，亦下嫁於諸侯...猶執婦道，以成肅雍之德。 — Though a king's daughter, she still marries down to a lord and yet keeps the way of a wife, achieving solemn and harmonious virtue.

items.text: Serve your parents-in-law zealously and humbly; nurse them in sickness, taste their medicine, and handle funeral help yourself.
items.quote: 姑涼國太夫人寢疾，比喪及葬，主奉養，蚤夜不解帶，親自嘗藥。 — When her mother-in-law fell ill until death and burial, she served her without loosening her sash at night and tasted the medicine herself.

items.text: Put away a wife who is proud toward your parents and hand her over to the magistrate.
items.quote: 為婦若此，為夫者宜棄之，為有司者治其罪可也。 — For a wife like this, the husband should divorce her, and the magistrate may punish her crime.
items.conflict: Divorce for filial rudeness conflicts with Christ's limiting divorce to sexual immorality (Matthew 19:9).

items.text: Let food and clothing come after the elders, even for servants and concubines.
items.quote: 雖婢妾，衣服飲食必後長者。 — Even maidservants and concubines must come after elders in clothing and food.

items.text: Serve the principal wife as a subject serves his ruler, keep your due place, and never use your husband's or son's influence to slight her.
items.quote: 妾事女君，猶臣事君也...況敢挾其主父與子之勢，陵慢其女君乎？ — A concubine serves the mistress as a subject serves his ruler; how dare she rely on her husband's or son's influence to slight the mistress?
items.conflict: Concubinage conflicts with Genesis 2:24 and Matthew 19:5, one man and one wife.

items.text: Choose for your child a teacher and nurse who is broad-minded, kind, gentle, respectful, careful, and sparing of speech.
items.quote: 必求其寬裕、慈惠、溫良、恭敬、慎而寡言者，使為子師。 — They must seek one who is broad-minded, kind, gentle, respectful, careful, and sparing of words to be the child's teacher.

items.text: Guard and feed the child in your care as a mother would; do not betray him for reward or fear, even to the point of death.
items.quote: 夫見利而反上者逆，畏死而棄義者，亂也...妾不能生而令公子禽矣！ — To turn on one's lord for gain is rebellion; to abandon duty for fear of death is disorder; I cannot let the young lord be captured while I live.

items.text: Honor the legal mother according to her rank; do not exalt a birth mother above the wife of your father.
items.quote: 尊其所生為太后，而以嫡母為太妃。 — He honored the one who bore him as empress dowager, but made the legal mother only dowager consort.

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷五 (子下) · 26 … 4

items.text: Do not leave your dead parent unburied, and do not delay the burial to choose a lucky site or day for your own advantage.
items.quote: 孝子何忍委其親不葬而求利己哉？ — How can a filial child bear to abandon his parent unburied in order to seek profit for himself?
items.conflict: Divination is forbidden; God alone rules life and death.

items.text: Commit your parent's body to the earth; if you cannot bring it home, bury it where death occurred rather than burning it.
items.quote: 即所亡之地而葬之，不猶愈於毀焚乎？ — To bury them in the place where they died is still better than destroying and burning them.

items.text: Keep a dead father's admonitions, and do not cast them off in your own conduct.
items.quote: 余廢先人之戒，其何以訓人？ — I have cast aside my father's command; how can I teach others?

items.text: Fulfil your departed parents' calling and preserve their work; this is a deeper filiality than burying and sacrificing alone.
items.quote: 能成其先人之誌，不墜其業者也 — Being able to fulfil their forebears' aims and not let their work fall.

items.text: Rise early, labor diligently, and in every station avoid arrogance, rebellion, and strife, so as not to disgrace your parents.
items.quote: 夙興夜寐，無忝爾所生 — Rise early and go to bed late; do not shame those who gave you life.

items.text: Do not be content merely to feed them; anticipate their wishes, carry out their will, and guide them to what is right.
items.quote: 先意承誌，諭父母於道 — Anticipate their will, receive their intent, and lead parents to the Way.

items.text: Live so uprightly that your parents are called blessed; the people's praise, not just offerings, is the proof of filial love.
items.quote: 國人稱願，然曰：幸哉，有子如此！所謂孝也已 — The people all say: 'Happy the parents who have such a son!' This is called filial.

items.text: Treat your body as your parents' bequest; be reverent at home, loyal to a ruler, faithful to friends, and brave in battle, lest shame fall on them.
items.quote: 身也者，父母之遺體也。行父母之遺體，敢不敬乎？ — The body is the parents' bequest; how dare you not be reverent in using it?

items.text: Teach daughters as well as sons; give them a moral and literary education, not only domestic work.
items.quote: 但教男而不教女，不亦蔽於彼此之教乎？ — To teach only boys and not girls is to be blind in either direction.

items.text: Serve your husband as your lord; keep purity, careful speech, modest neatness, and diligence in household work.
items.quote: 殊不知夫主之不可不事，禮義之不可不存 — They hardly know that a husband must be served and propriety must be kept.

items.text: Shield your step-parent from harm and take blame on yourself to save them.
items.quote: 初在左右，心恐繼母去置奩中，乃曰：「初坐之。」 — The daughter, fearing her stepmother had placed them there, said: 'I am to blame.'

items.text: Love your stepchild as your own child and refuse to let her bear the blame for you.
items.quote: 繼母又曰：「兒但讓耳，實妾取之。」 — The stepmother said: 'The child only yields; I really took them.'

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷八 (妻上) · 10 … 1

items.text: Remain faithful to your husband after death; do not remarry or turn to another man.
items.quote: 婦人之義，一往而不改，以全貞信之節 — A wife's duty is one unchanging devotion, preserving chastity and faithfulness.
items.conflict: Scripture permits widows to remarry (1 Cor 7:39-40; 1 Tim 5:14).

items.text: Keep the promise you made to your husband to care for his mother; do not set it aside.
items.quote: 夫行時屬妾以其老母，妾既許諾之……許人以諾而不能信，將何以立於世？ — My husband entrusted his old mother to me; having promised, how can I stand before the world if I do not keep my word?

items.text: Serve your husband's aged mother to the end of her days; let your care not slacken.
items.quote: 婦乃養姑不衰，慈愛愈固……遂使養其姑二十八年 — She cared for her mother-in-law without weakening; she served her for twenty-eight years.

items.text: When she dies, spend your estate to bury her and keep the offerings.
items.quote: 姑八十余，以天年終，盡賣其田宅財物以葬之，終奉祭祀 — When her mother-in-law died at over eighty, she sold her fields and house to bury her and continued the sacrifices.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead conflict with Deut 18:10-12; Heb 9:27.

items.text: Do not abandon your young child; stay alive and rear him though you are bereaved.
items.quote: 不忍幼弱之重孤也 — I could not bear to make the little one doubly orphaned.

items.text: Rear and educate your son until he becomes a person of name and worth.
items.quote: 教養善果，至於成名 — She reared and taught Shanguo until he won a name.

items.text: Let no man touch your body; accept death rather than defilement.
items.quote: 義不以身受辱寇虜也 — Righteousness forbids my body to suffer disgrace from bandits.

items.text: When your husband's house is swept away, do not abandon it; seek a son to rear as his heir.
items.quote: 聽使乞子，養為曹氏後 — She was allowed to seek a son to rear as Cao's heir.

items.text: To make your widowhood irrevocable, cut off a lock or ear and cast it into his coffin as a vow before the spirits.
items.quote: 房氏操刀割左耳，投之棺中，仍曰：鬼神有知，相期泉壤 — Fang cut off her left ear and threw it into the coffin, saying: If the spirits know, we will meet below the grave.
items.conflict: Deut 14:1 forbids cutting the body for the dead; Deut 18:10-12 forbids seeking the dead; the body is the temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Cor 6:19).

items.text: Do not be jealous of your husband's concubines or their sons; let the house flourish without your envy.
items.quote: 皆美其無妒忌之行——婦人之美，無如不妒矣 — All praise her freedom from jealousy; no beauty in a wife surpasses freedom from jealousy.
items.conflict: Polygamy and concubinage conflict with Gen 2:24 and 1 Cor 7:2.

items.text: If another man seizes your hand or arm, cut it off rather than allow any part of you to be dishonored.
items.quote: 不可以一手並汙吾身 — I will not let one hand defile my whole body.
items.conflict: Self-mutilation is not required for purity; moral purity comes from the heart (Matt 15:18-20), and the body is God's temple (1 Cor 6:19-20).

items.text: Do not disgrace your ancestors; cultivate your virtue.
items.quote: 無忝爾祖，聿修厥德 — Bring no shame to your ancestors; cultivate your virtue.

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷三 (父母 父 母) · 11 … 34

items.text: Train them from earliest childhood, make them obey and stop when told, correct wrong rather than hiding it, and be dignified as well as kind.
items.quote: 便加教誨，使為則為，使止則止…父母威嚴而有慈，則子女畏慎而生孝矣。 — Teach them as soon as understanding dawns; make them do what is right and stop what is wrong. Parents’ dignity and kindness produce obedient, filial children.

items.text: Do not let private fondness make you favor one child over another; love the worthy and pity the dull.
items.quote: 賢俊者自可賞愛，頑魯者亦當矜憐。有偏寵者，雖欲以厚之，更所以禍之。 — Cherish the worthy and pity the dull; partial love, though meant for good, brings harm.

items.text: Teach an unfilial or disrespectful daughter-in-law; rebuke her if she will not learn; if she still will not amend, have your son send her away, and do not either hide her faults or over-punish her.
items.quote: 子婦未孝未敬，勿庸疾怨，姑教之。若不可教，而後怒之。 — If a son’s wife is not filial or respectful, do not nurse resentment; teach her. If she cannot be taught, rebuke her.
items.conflict: Christ allows divorce only for sexual immorality (Matt. 19:9), not for a daughter-in-law's disobedience to her in-laws.

items.text: Serve your father's affairs reverently; do not wound his heart.
items.quote: 子弗祗服厥父事，大傷厥考心。 — If a son does not reverently perform his father’s work, he greatly wounds his father’s heart.

items.text: Father, love and care for your children; do not hate them.
items.quote: 於父不能字厥子，乃疾厥子。 — If a father cannot love his son and instead hates him.

items.text: Do not let love become indulgence; teach as you love, for a doting mother ruins her child.
items.quote: 慈母敗子。愛而不教，使淪於不肖。 — A doting mother ruins her son; love without teaching lets him sink into folly.

items.text: While carrying your child, guard your eyes, ears, mouth, food, and posture from evil so that the child may be well formed.
items.quote: 目不視惡色，耳不聽淫聲，口不出敖言…不食邪味，席不正不坐。 — Do not look at evil sights, listen to lewd sounds, speak proud words, eat improper food, or sit untidily.

items.text: Choose a wholesome place for your child's upbringing and keep your word to him, so he learns truthfulness.
items.quote: 此真可以居子矣！…今適有知而欺之，是教之不信。 — This is the right place for my son! … Now that he can understand, to deceive him is to teach him untruth.

items.text: Support your stepchild's education by your own labor.
items.quote: 繼母隨方進之長安，織履，以資方進遊學。 — His stepmother followed him to Chang’an and wove sandals to pay for his studies.

items.text: Refuse gifts from your child that come from neglect of study, from bribery, or from misuse of office; teach him integrity.
items.quote: 汝不讀書，而田獵如是，吾無望矣！竟不食其膳。 — Since you do not study but hunt like this, I have no hope; she refused to eat his food.

items.text: Watch over your son's official conduct; praise him when he is just and merciful, and refuse food when he is not.
items.quote: 母輒問不疑，有所平反，活幾何人耶？…母怒，為不食。故不疑為吏嚴而不殘。 — His mother asked how many he had exonerated… if none, she was angry and would not eat; so he was strict but not cruel.

items.text: Do not bring a later wife into a household where you already have children and grandchildren, lest she ruin the house.
items.quote: 時俗希不以後妻敗家者。遂不娶。 — Few later wives fail to ruin a house; he did not remarry.
items.conflict: Scripture permits remarriage after a spouse's death or divorce (1 Cor. 7:39; Matt. 5:32); a father may remarry with wisdom and guard his house without an absolute prohibition.

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷三 (父母 父 母) · 50 … 28

items.text: Teach your daughter before marriage to make submission and chastity her first duties, and do not aid her in defying her husband's family.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 卷三 (父母 父 母) 50 … 28
items.quote: 女未嫁，不能誨也。既嫁，為之援，使挾己以淩其婿家。 — If you cannot teach her before marriage, after marriage you may aid her to bully her husband's family.

items.text: Do not let laziness, gambling, drink, love of money, or private family keep you from supporting your parents.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 卷三 (父母 父 母) 50 … 28
items.quote: 好貨財，私妻子，不顧父母之養 — Loving goods and private wife and children, neglecting parents' support.

items.text: Do not follow sensual desires or fight and quarrel, so that you disgrace or endanger your parents.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 卷三 (父母 父 母) 50 … 28
items.quote: 從耳目之欲，以為父母戮；好勇鬥狠以危父母 — Indulging sensual desires disgraces parents; fighting endangers parents.

items.text: Serve your parents with reverence, not merely by feeding them as you feed animals.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 卷三 (父母 父 母) 50 … 28
items.quote: 今之孝者，是謂能養。至於犬馬，皆能有養。不敬，何以別乎？ — Now filial piety means feeding; even dogs and horses are fed; without reverence, what difference is there?

items.text: Obey your parents' commands promptly and announce your departures and returns.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 卷三 (父母 父 母) 50 … 28
items.quote: 父母之命勿逆勿怠。出必告，反必面。 — Do not disobey or neglect parents' commands; when going out, tell them; on returning, present yourself.

items.text: As a daughter-in-law, keep no private goods or savings; do not lend or give privately without the household's leave.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 卷三 (父母 父 母) 50 … 28
items.quote: 子婦無私貨，無私畜，無私器。不敢私假，不敢私與。 — Daughters-in-law have no private goods, savings, or utensils; they dare not give or lend privately.
items.conflict: A wife retains personal property rights; parents-in-law have no warrant to strip her of all private goods.

items.text: Do not accept honors, carriages, or riches that would set you above your father or elder brother.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 卷三 (父母 父 母) 50 … 28
items.quote: 不敢以富貴加於父兄 — Do not set wealth or rank above father or elder brother.

items.text: Even in danger, do not cease to send word and comfort to your parents.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 卷三 (父母 父 母) 50 … 28
items.quote: 乃可無我，此事不容暫廢。 — I may be lost, but this matter cannot be suspended for a moment.

items.text: When your parents are ill, set aside personal ease, music, and ordinary pleasures, and give yourself to caring for them until recovery.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 卷三 (父母 父 母) 50 … 28
items.quote: 父母有疾，冠者不櫛，行不翔，言不惰，琴瑟不禦。 — When parents are ill, do not comb, walk briskly, speak idle words, or play music.

items.text: When your parents die, mourn with grief and offer the ancestral sacrifices with reverence.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 卷三 (父母 父 母) 50 … 28
items.quote: 喪則致其哀，祭則致其嚴。 — In mourning show grief; in sacrifice show awe.
items.conflict: Ancestor sacrifices are religious rites owed to God alone.

items.text: Use your income first to support aged parents, even to the exclusion of wife and children.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 卷三 (父母 父 母) 50 … 28
items.quote: 縣祿唯供養母一身，不以及妻子。 — He used his official salary only to support his mother, not wife and children.
items.conflict: Scripture requires a man to provide for his own household and not neglect wife and children.

items.text: When a parent is near death, bow to the North Star and ask to die in the parent's place.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 卷三 (父母 父 母) 50 … 28
items.quote: 每稽顙北辰，求以身代 — He bowed to the North Star and begged to take his father's place.
items.conflict: Prayer and worship belong to God alone, not to the stars or created things.

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷五 (子下) · 5 … 25

items.text: When father and mother are angry and beat you until you bleed, do not dare to resent them; rise again in reverence and filial love.
items.quote: 父母怒，不說而撻之流血，不敢疾怨，起敬起孝。 — When father and mother are angry and beat you till you bleed, do not resent it; rise in reverence and filial devotion.

items.text: Serve your parents with concealment and no offense; when they err, remonstrate privately, not defiantly, and if they will not hear, follow them weeping.
items.quote: 事親有隱而無犯。又曰：父母有過，諫而不逆。又曰：三諫而不聽則號泣而隨之 — Serve parents with concealment and no offense; when father and mother have faults, remonstrate but do not oppose; if three remonstrances are not heeded, weep and follow.

items.text: Give the good to your parents and take the blame yourself; say with the poem, 'My mother is wise and good; I am without virtue.'
items.quote: 孝子善則稱親，過則歸己。《凱風》曰：“母氏聖善，我無令人。” — A filial son ascribes good to father and mother and faults to himself. The Kaifeng says: 'My mother is wise and good; I am without virtue.'

items.text: If your parents do not love you, blame yourself and serve them with such sincere reverence that they come to trust and yield.
items.quote: 子孝矣而父母不愛，如之何？曰：責己而已。 — What if a son is filial but father and mother do not love him? Blame yourself.

items.text: When your parents are ill, do not loosen your sash; taste the medicine and treatments yourself and stay by them day and night.
items.quote: 父母有疾，衣不解帶，湯藥必親嘗。 — When father and mother were ill, he did not loosen his sash and tasted the medicines himself.

items.text: When a stepmother is harsh, drives you out, or falsely accuses you, do not leave, resent her, or expose her; continue attending her morning and evening.
items.quote: 由是倫遂不聽李氏之譖。及倫卒，衍事李氏益謹。 — After that Lun no longer listened to Lady Li's slander; when Lun died, Yan served Lady Li even more carefully.

items.text: Support and visit your stepmother even when you are rich or aged, and do not speak of your own old age.
items.quote: 太尉胡廣年八十，繼母在堂，朝夕贍省，旁無幾杖，言不稱老。 — Grand Commandant Hu Guang, at eighty, with his stepmother still in the hall, attended her morning and evening; with no staff beside him, he did not speak of his own old age.

items.text: If your parents are displeased with your wife, put her away; if they approve her, keep performing the conjugal rites all your life.
items.quote: 子甚宜其妻父母不說，出。子不宜其妻，父母曰：‘是善事我，’子行夫婦之禮焉，沒身不衰。 — If a son is very pleased with his wife but father and mother are displeased, put her away; if he is not pleased with her but they say she serves us well, he should render conjugal duty all his life.
items.conflict: Genesis 2:24; Matthew 19:6 — a man shall leave father and mother and hold fast to his wife.

items.text: If poverty cannot support both your mother and your child, do not spare the child; a mother once lost cannot be had again.
items.quote: 貧乏不能供給，共汝埋子。子可再有，母不可再得。 — Poverty cannot provide for both; bury our child with me. A child can be had again, but a mother cannot be had again.
items.conflict: Exodus 20:13; Matthew 18:6 — do not murder; do not cause little ones to stumble.

items.text: Serve a father-appointed foster mother as your own mother all her life, and mourn her three years as a mother.
items.quote: 慈母如母……若是，則生養之，終其身如母，死則喪之三年如母 — A foster mother is as a mother... nourish and serve her, treat her as mother all her life, and mourn her three years as mother.

items.text: Bury your parent within the appointed months; until burial, keep mourning dress, eat gruel, dwell in the mourning hut, and sleep on straw and a clod.
items.quote: 未葬不變服，啜粥，居倚廬，寢苫枕塊 — Before burial, do not change mourning dress; sip congee, dwell in the mourning hut, sleep on straw and clod.

items.text: If a parent died before you could serve them, honor them by carving a wooden image and serving it.
items.quote: 丁蘭者，母早亡，不及養，乃刻木而事之 — Ding Lan, whose mother died early and whom he could not serve, carved wood and served it.
items.conflict: Second Commandment; Deuteronomy 27:15 — no carved image for worship.

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷一 (治家) · 29 … 44

items.text: Manage the household entrusted to you as a public trust; keep account of all income and spending, and take nothing for yourself.
items.quote: 弘微經紀生業，事若在公。一錢、尺帛，出入皆有文薄。 — He managed the household as if it were a public trust; every coin and cloth was recorded.

items.text: When the one whose house you kept dies leaving property, do not take it; bury them from your own salary.
items.quote: 弘微一物不取，自以私祿營葬。 — He took nothing and buried the dead with his own salary.

items.text: Do not secretly scheme to divide your husband from his brothers or break up the common household.
items.quote: 君良妻欲其異居，乃密取庭樹鳥雛交置巢中... 破家賊，乃汝耶！ — Junliang's wife wanted to live apart, so she secretly made the birds fight; he cried: 'Home-wrecker, it was you!'

items.text: Bear with one another when provision or courtesy is unequal; forbearance keeps the clan harmonious.
items.quote: 茍能相與忍之，則常睦雍矣。 — If you can bear with one another, the family will always be harmonious.

items.text: Give your father morning and evening attendance, greeting him early and settling him at night.
items.quote: 晨省於中門之北...昏定於中門之北。 — They made morning greetings and evening settling north of the inner gate.

items.text: Give your sons and nephews daily instruction in the classics and household management, and in famine make them eat plainly.
items.quote: 命子弟一人執經史立燭前...遇饑歲，則諸子皆蔬食。 — He ordered a son to read classics by candle... in famine the sons ate vegetables.

items.text: For orphaned or widowed kinswomen, even distant ones, arrange a marriage promptly rather than waiting for a rich dowry.
items.quote: 姑姊妹侄有孤嫠者，雖疏遠，必為擇婿嫁之；必待資裝豐備，何如嫁不失時。 — For orphaned or widowed aunts, sisters and nieces, however distant, find husbands; why wait for rich dowry?
items.needs_role: orphaned or widowed female kinswoman (姑姊妹侄)

items.text: Pool the yields of fields and houses and salaries into one common store and give daily shares, so no private hoarding causes resentment.
items.quote: 田園邸舍所收及有官者俸祿，皆聚之一庫，計口日給餅飯。 — Field and house produce and salaries were pooled in one store and given daily by mouth.

items.text: Teach your sons that a single arrow breaks but a bundle cannot; be of one mind and one strength.
items.quote: 單者易折，眾者難摧。戮力一心，然後社稷可固。 — A single one breaks easily; many are hard to break. Join strength and one heart, then the house is secure.

items.text: Do not slander or supplant an elder brother, for by destroying your own family you destroy yourself.
items.quote: 汝喪而宗室，於人何有？人亦於汝何有？ — You ruin your own house; what are you to others, and what are they to you?

items.text: Love and honor your parents above all; otherwise love and honor of others is against virtue and courtesy.
items.quote: 不愛其親而愛他人者，謂之悖德；不敬其親而敬他人者，謂之悖禮。 — To love others but not your parents is against virtue; to honor others but not your parents is against courtesy.

items.text: Support your poor cousins and share even thin porridge with them, eating the same yourself without distaste.
items.quote: 中表貧乏者，皆收養之。以二石米為薄粥，僅得遍焉，躬自同之。 — He took in poor cousins, made thin porridge with two pecks of rice, shared it all and ate the same.

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷九 (妻下) · 23 … 14

items.text: Give your husband faithful counsel and warn him when his plans are wrong.
items.quote: 數規諫明帝，辭意款備 — Repeatedly she admonished Mingdi with thorough and sincere words.

items.text: Urge your husband to grow daily in knowledge and virtue rather than turn back halfway.
items.quote: 夫子積學，當日知其所亡，以就懿德 — In your studies grow daily in knowledge to attain virtue.

items.text: Be loyal to your husband and lay down your life for him rather than betray him.
items.quote: 古之節婦，有以死徇其夫者，況敢庸奴其夫乎？ — Of old, chaste wives died for their husbands; how could they treat their husbands as slaves?
items.conflict: The Sixth Commandment forbids taking innocent life, including one's own; God calls a wife to loyalty, not to self-destruction.

items.text: Work with your own hands to care for your husband's parents, and do not abandon them in old age.
items.quote: 妻常躬勤養姑 — The wife herself constantly labored to care for her mother-in-law.

items.text: Obey your parents-in-law absolutely; even when they are wrong, do not dispute right and wrong.
items.quote: 姑云爾而非，猶宜順命。勿得違戾是非，爭分曲直 — Even if she says a wrong thing, still obey; do not dispute right and wrong.
items.conflict: We must obey God rather than men; no human authority may command what God forbids.

items.text: If your husband's parents do wrong, remonstrate gently with them.
items.quote: 然則舅姑有過，婦亦可幾諫也 — Thus when parents-in-law have faults, a wife may also remonstrate gently.

items.text: Have no private goods, savings, or tools; do not lend or give anything without your parents-in-law's leave.
items.quote: 子婦無私貨，無私蓄，無私器，不敢私假，不敢私與 — A son's wife has no private goods, savings, or utensils, and may not lend or give privately.
items.conflict: The Eighth Commandment protects private property; Scripture gives a wife lawful control over goods.

items.text: Be kind to your daughter-in-law; give her rest when she labors and correct her patiently.
items.quote: 子婦有勤勞之事，雖甚愛之，姑縱之而寧數休之 — When your daughter-in-law has heavy work, give her rest often.

items.text: Honor your maternal uncle as you would your mother; stand by him as kin.
items.quote: 我見舅氏，如母存焉 — When I see my uncle, it is as if my mother were alive.

items.text: Provide for your nephew or niece in need, even from your own mouth.
items.quote: 頰邊貯飯以活外甥周翼 — He stored food in his cheek to keep his nephew Zhou Yi alive.

items.text: Return and care for your aged mother; do not abandon her even in famine.
items.quote: 君有老母，不可以不歸 — You have an old mother; you cannot fail to return.

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷九 (妻下) · 2 … 22

items.text: Do not be jealous; accept your husband's other wives and concubines, and yield the chief place to the first wife and her son.
items.quote: 以叔隗為內子，而己下之 — She made Shu Wei the principal wife and placed herself below her.
items.conflict: Polygamy and concubinage are sin; marriage is one man and one woman (Gen 2:24; Matt 19:5–6).

items.text: Serve your husband's mother with care and do not neglect her.
items.quote: 女宗之養姑愈謹 — Nü Zong served her mother-in-law with even greater care.

items.text: Help your husband to a good name; correct and warn him when he neglects his duty.
items.quote: 又當輔佐君子，成其令名 — She should also assist her lord and complete his good name.

items.text: Be frugal and plain in clothing and household goods; do not pursue luxury or display.
items.quote: 婦人固以儉約為美，不以侈麗為美也 — A woman is praised for frugality, not for extravagance.

items.text: Rise early and go to bed late; do your household tasks thoroughly and do not shun hard work.
items.quote: 晚寢早作，勿憚夙夜 — Go to bed late, rise early; do not dread morning or evening.

items.text: Honor and attend your husband with chaste, modest respect, as to a guest.
items.quote: 冀缺之妻饁其夫，相待如賓 — Ji Que's wife carried food to her husband; they treated each other like guests.

items.text: Perform the prescribed ancestral sacrifices faithfully.
items.quote: 《采蘋》、《采蘩》，美夫人能奉祭祀 — The Cai Pin and Cai Fan praise the wife who can serve in the sacrifices.
items.conflict: Offerings and prayers to the dead are forbidden; worship God alone (Deut 26:14; Heb 9:27).

items.text: Teach your son that a noble house works with its hands and does not excuse idleness.
items.quote: 吾冀而朝夕修我曰：必無廢先人 — I hoped you would daily urge me: Do not neglect the ancestors.

items.text: Do not share in your husband's wrongful pleasures; refuse them and admonish him.
items.quote: 齊桓公好淫樂，衛姬為之不聽 — Duke Huan of Qi loved licentious music; Wei Ji, for his sake, would not listen to it.

items.text: Urge him to pursue his calling rather than settle in comfort and ease.
items.quote: 行也，懷與安，實敗名 — Go; indulgence and ease indeed ruin a name.

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷六 (女 孫 伯叔父 姪) · 5 … 24

items.text: Support aged or ailing parents; work day and night to provide for them, and do not abandon them to marry.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 6 (女 孫 伯叔父 姪) 5–24
items.quote: 晝采樵，夜紡績，以供養。父母俱卒，親營殯葬 — She gathered firewood by day and spun by night to support them; when they died she buried them.

items.text: Offer yourself as a servant to ransom your father from punishment, so he may live anew.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 6 (女 孫 伯叔父 姪) 5–24
items.quote: 妾願入身為官婢，以贖父刑罪 — I wish to become a government slave to redeem my father's punishment.

items.text: Suffer death rather than dishonor; keep your chastity unspotted.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 6 (女 孫 伯叔父 姪) 5–24
items.quote: 吾寧就死，義不受辱 — I would rather die than suffer dishonor.
items.conflict: Do not take your own life; suicide is self-murder. Trust God in danger.

items.text: Avenge your father's murder; do not share the same sky with his killer.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 6 (女 孫 伯叔父 姪) 5–24
items.quote: 父母之仇，不與共戴天 — A parent's enemy cannot be allowed to share the same sky.
items.conflict: Leave vengeance to God; do not murder, even for a parent.

items.text: Recover a dead parent's body and bury it, then cut your hair, disfigure yourself, and dwell by the grave.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 6 (女 孫 伯叔父 姪) 5–24
items.quote: 剪發壞形，廬於墓所 — She cut her hair, disfigured herself, and dwelt at the grave.
items.conflict: Honoring and burying a parent is right, but self-mutilation is not commanded; our bodies are God's temple.

items.text: Care for the grandparent who raised you; refuse office so you can support her in her last years and bury her when she dies.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 6 (女 孫 伯叔父 姪) 5–24
items.quote: 臣無祖母，無以至今日；祖母無臣，無以終余年 — Without my grandmother I would not be here; without me she cannot finish her years.

items.text: Do not neglect virtue, for to be slack in virtue is to forget your ancestors.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 6 (女 孫 伯叔父 姪) 5–24
items.quote: 無忘爾祖，聿修厥德 — Forget not your ancestors; cultivate their virtue.

items.text: Keep your ancestors' land and houses; do not sell or give them to the powerful.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 6 (女 孫 伯叔父 姪) 5–24
items.quote: 今尺寸土，皆先人舊物，非吾等所有，安可奉權臣邪 — Every inch of land is our ancestors' old possession, not ours; how can we hand it to a powerful minister?

items.text: Seek your grandfather's healing by praying to Buddha and bowing before scriptures.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 6 (女 孫 伯叔父 姪) 5–24
items.quote: 晝夜讀佛經禮拜，以祈福佑 — Day and night he read Buddhist scriptures and bowed in worship to seek blessing.
items.conflict: Prayer belongs to God alone; do not seek healing from Buddha.

items.text: Care for a brother's child as your own, and in danger protect a dead brother's orphan even at great cost.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 6 (女 孫 伯叔父 姪) 5–24
items.quote: 力不能兩活，仲不可以絕類 — If both cannot live, my brother's line must not be cut off.

items.text: Raise and instruct an orphaned nephew; correct him gently, even at your own pain.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 6 (女 孫 伯叔父 姪) 5–24
items.quote: 恭養孤幼，教誨學問，有不如法，輒反用杖自箠以感悟之 — He raised the orphan, taught him learning, and when he erred he struck himself with the rod to move him.

items.text: When dividing family property with nephews, take the poorer shares, and if they fall into want, relieve them.
items.citation: Jia Fan, 6 (女 孫 伯叔父 姪) 5–24
items.quote: 田廬取其荒頓者...弟子數破其產，輒復賑給 — He took the neglected fields and huts; when they repeatedly ruined their property, he relieved them.

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷一 (治家) · 1 … 28

items.text: Husbands and wives, each keep to your proper place: she within the household, he in public affairs.
items.quote: 女正位乎內，男正位乎外 — The woman's right place is within; the man's right place is outside.

items.text: Revere your parents as the household's strict rulers.
items.quote: 家人有嚴君焉，父母之謂也 — In a household there are strict rulers: father and mother.

items.text: Be kind to your children and instruct them.
items.quote: 父慈而教 — The father is kind and teaches.

items.text: Love your younger siblings and be a friend to them.
items.quote: 兄愛而友 — The elder brother loves and befriends.

items.text: Respect your older siblings and obey them.
items.quote: 弟敬而順 — The younger brother respects and follows.

items.text: Be gentle and righteous toward your wife.
items.quote: 夫和而義 — The husband is gentle and upright.

items.text: Be gentle and upright toward your husband.
items.quote: 妻柔而正 — The wife is gentle and correct.

items.text: Be kind and yielding toward your daughter-in-law.
items.quote: 姑慈而從 — The mother-in-law is kind and yielding.

items.text: Obey your mother-in-law and speak to her gently.
items.quote: 婦聽而婉 — The daughter-in-law is obedient and gentle.
items.conflict: A wife's primary human obligation is to her husband, not to his mother (Gen 2:24; Eph 5:22).

items.text: Keep strict separation between the sexes in the household: do not sit together, share a rack or towel, or pass things directly from hand to hand.
items.quote: 男女不雜坐，不同椸枷，不同巾櫛，不親授受 — Men and women do not sit together, use the same rack, share towel or comb, or hand things directly.

items.text: Honor your father's dying instruction: cancel the debts as he commanded, and do not take repayment.
items.quote: 遺令焚削文契... 諸子從敕，竟不肯受 — He left a command to burn the loan contracts; his sons obeyed and would not accept repayment.

items.text: Support your clan and neighbors out of your abundance and help settle their disputes generously.
items.quote: 賑贍宗族，恩加鄉閭 — He relieved and supported his clan and extended kindness to his neighbors.

heading: 家範 Jia Fan · Sima Guang · 家範 卷六 (女 孫 伯叔父 姪) · 25 … 16

items.text: Preserve your deceased brother's only son; his line must not be allowed to end.
items.quote: 吾弟早亡，唯有一息，理不可絕，止應自棄我兒耳。 — My younger brother died early; his only son's line must not end; we ought to abandon our own son.
items.conflict: Violates the parent's duty to his own child; parents may not abandon or expose a child for clan succession.

items.text: Mourn the uncle who raised you as a parent for three years.
items.quote: 弟子綏服攸喪三年。 — His nephew Sui wore mourning for Deng You for three years.
items.conflict: Ritual mourning to the dead can become ancestor veneration; Christians do not perform meritorious rites for the dead.

items.text: Do not abandon your orphaned nephews or sister's sons in famine; feed them even by going hungry yourself.
items.quote: 食訖，以飯著兩頰邊還，吐與二兒。 — After eating, he put rice in his cheeks, returned, and fed the two boys with it.

items.text: Do not grow weary in seeking justice and providing for an uncle in prison; sell your house if needed.
items.quote: 資產既盡，賣宅以充之。肇之諸子倦怠，惟昭先無有懈息，如是七載。 — His property exhausted, he sold the house; the other sons tired, but he never slackened for seven years.

items.text: Serve your father's younger brother as you serve your own father, with respectful dress and daily greeting.
items.quote: 事諸父如父，禮也。 — Serve all your father's brothers as your father; this is propriety.

items.text: Do not hold anger or grudges against a younger brother; love him and seek his honor and prosperity.
items.quote: 仁人之於弟也，不藏怒焉，不宿怨焉，親愛之而已矣。親之欲其貴也，愛之欲其富也。 — A benevolent man toward his younger brother hides no anger, stores no grudge; he loves him, wanting his honor and wealth.

items.text: Give a younger brother a generous share of the estate; if he becomes destitute, share again.
items.quote: 田宅財物盡與弟。而弟盡破其產，式輒復分與弟者數矣。 — He gave his brother all the land and goods; when the brother ruined his estate, he repeatedly gave again.

items.text: Do not answer an elder brother from bed; rise, dress, and stand straight before answering.
items.quote: 他先不答應，下床穿上衣服，端端正正地站好，然後才答應。 — He did not answer at once; he rose, dressed, stood straight, and only then answered.

items.text: If your elder brother is doing wrong, remonstrate with him and work to restore his integrity.
items.quote: 錢沒了可以再掙，但當官如果貪贓枉法，就會受到懲處，一輩子都完了。 — Money can be earned again, but if an official takes bribes he is ruined forever.

items.text: Stay and nurse a sick elder brother through pestilence; do not flee when others withdraw.
items.quote: 親自扶持，晝夜不眠。守人所不能守，行人所不能行。 — He personally supported his brother day and night without sleep; he kept what others cannot keep, did what others cannot do.

items.text: Yield succession and inheritance to one another rather than contend.
items.quote: 父欲立叔齊。及父卒，叔齊讓伯夷。伯夷曰：父命也。遂逃去。叔齊亦不肯立而逃之。 — Their father wanted Shuqi to succeed; when the father died, Shuqi yielded to Boyi. Boyi said, 'Father commanded it,' and fled; Shuqi also refused and fled.

items.text: Do not let sisters-in-law become a place of quarreling; act with self-denial and raise one another's sons as your own.
items.quote: 娣姒者，多爭之地也……若能恕己而行，換子而撫，則此患不生矣。 — Sisters-in-law are a place of many quarrels; if you act by self-denial and raise each other's sons, this trouble will not arise.
